pretreatments.description: Harvesting and packaging of Miscanthus (Miscanthus sacchariflorus) from Jiangsu province, China.
Air drying of harvested Miscanthus at room temperature.
Breaking of Miscanthus with a paper cutter.
Screening and collection of Miscanthus particles passing through a 20-mesh sieve and retained by a 40-mesh sieve.
Storage of collected Miscanthus in a plastic vacuum bag to prevent degradation.
Hydrothermal pretreatment performed in a 100 mL stainless steel reactor with a Teflon vessel.
Addition of 2.5 g of Miscanthus and 25 mL of distilled water to the reactor.
Continuous mixture provided by 20 rpm rotation.
Setting of pretreatment temperature at 125, 150, 175 and 200 °C, respectively.
Cooling of reactors to room temperature using cold water after a 30 min pretreatment period.
Filtration for solid-liquid separation and recovery of Miscanthus.
Washing of pretreated Miscanthus with distilled water.
Drying and storage of the pretreated Miscanthus in a vacuum plastic bag.
Anaerobic digestion performed in batch reactors with digested pig manure as inoculum.
Enzymatic hydrolysis using commercial cellulase concentrated solution from Sigma-Aldrich with sodium acetate buffer (50 mM, pH 5.0).
Incubation of enzyme hydrolysis at 50 °C in a 50 °C incubator shaker at 190 rpm for 3–72 h.
Deactivation of enzyme by incubation in a water bath at 100 °C for 10 min.
Analysis of cellulose hydrolysis rate by HPLC with refractive index detector and NH2P-50 4E column.
Fourier transform infrared spectrophotometry (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Nicolet 5700) to analyze changes in functional groups.
X-ray diffraction (Bruker, D8 Advance) to analyze cellulose crystallinity.
Scanning electron microscopy (Phenom, Pro) to analyze surface structure changes.
